action_summary: Adapt the shared Python SWE suite runner to native pytest when needed; preserve stdlib-only execution and fail closed when test semantics cannot be provided. Pin the tested pytest runtime and its dependencies in the existing deterministic SWE kernel requirements. Adapt existing tracing to filter non-project frames so native-framework tracing does not spend its deadline resolving every library line.
causal_blocker: The shared software-engineering suite runner silently omits fixture and parameterized tests, allowing repair, audit, and localization paths to claim success against an incomplete suite.

expected_parent_change: Software-engineering callers sharing suite_argv execute pytest-dependent tests with the actual available framework, retain stdlib execution for compatible tests, and refuse unsupported suites when that framework is unavailable.
expected_parent_frontier_change: Software-engineering callers sharing suite_argv execute pytest-dependent tests with the actual available framework, retain stdlib execution for compatible tests, and refuse unsupported suites when that framework is unavailable.
stop_condition: Stop when fixture, parameterized, mixed unittest/pytest, unavailable-framework and no-test cases behave truthfully, existing stdlib controls still work, and measured latency and remaining limitations are reported without capability credit.
explicit_user_authorization: The user asked to reuse solutions already in Brain, tools, repositories or research and do the optimal work as fast as possible for advanced software engineering.
highest_leverage_scope: Highest-leverage candidate among the locally evaluated shared-runner repair routes; not a claim of universal global optimum.
measured_effect: Before implementation the shared runner returned 0 for a fixture suite on which native pytest returned 1. After implementation 30 focused regressions pass under pytest 8.4.2 and 9.2.0, and 96 repair/tracing tests pass under each; 55 relevant unittest tests pass without pytest. The hash-pinned SWE kernel installs on the tested Linux/Python 3.11 environment. Two unrelated existing integration contracts fail and are recorded below. Measurements are local, with no capability, terminal, or independent-verification credit.
falsification_condition: Any selected failing fixture or parametrized test is missed, unsupported pytest semantics are silently treated as green without pytest, a previously working stdlib control regresses, or the reported counts disagree with observed execution.

local_verification_summary.pytest_latency: 15 interleaved failing-fixture subprocesses: shared runner 235.31 ms median versus direct pytest 233.67 ms, with plugin autoload disabled.
local_verification_summary.trace_latency: Five native-fixture failing traces: fault-localizer 360.63 ms median (5 project events); provenance 328.15 ms median (9 events). An earlier pre-optimization trace took 22.56 s under concurrent load, so those observations are not a controlled speedup estimate.
